title: Perf run 20261020-1303
heading: No speed win found: seven ideas measured, none called, and the branch keeps no app change
meta: This speed run tried seven ideas against the moments a player waits on. Four were built and measured with interleaved A/Bs, two were stopped by probes before an A/B, and one was cut down by traces. No primary row was called faster, so no app change is kept. The PR carries only the loop's records: the run record, the ledger, the scoreboard, the A/B reports, the saved patches and a JIT probe. The branch is improve/20261020-1303 from base 4bdeb55; main did not move during the run. Every figure is from software rendering (SwiftShader) on a 4-vCPU VM, and each names the commits it compares.

needs.intro: Nothing here blocks the merge. The first item is information. The other three are owner rules or taste calls that stand in front of the biggest leads left; an answer lets a later run build them.

items.title: Information: the target (every primary row 1.2× faster) is not met
items.body: No change was kept, so the branch runs the base's app code and every primary row stays where the base left it. The step-2 A/B (4bdeb55 against the last base bd26e1c, 10 pairs) called no row either way. Two rows leaned slower there without being called: a shared game's first screen ×1.063 (6 of 10 pairs worse, pairs 0.84–1.20) and a pick ×1.031 (5 of 10, pairs 0.88–1.39). The only app diff between those commits is code these paths do not run, so the run read both as noise. The remaining large waits are bound by the GPU's first draw of each shader program under software rendering, which the code ideas left on the ledger cannot remove without one of the three changes below.

items.title: HF1: may the level focus wait for the pointer to settle (about 200 ms)?
items.body: Today the other levels step back as soon as the pointer is over a level. That fades the whole tower in the same frames as a pick or a move. Traces from this run's A/B data show the GPU time of a frame tracks its triangles: White's level-changing moves draw 76–86k triangles in 145–161 ms, against 35–52k in 93–118 ms on one level. If the focus waited for the pointer to rest on a level for about 150–250 ms, a click's picture would not carry the fade. The emphasis would then arrive one dwell later. Estimate, not measured: the player's move ×0.70–0.80 and a pick ×0.55–0.75. It is not built.
items.recommend: Allow a patch: the next speed run builds it with before-and-after interaction sheets and a move + pick A/B, and puts both in front of you before anything lands.

items.title: RW2: may a finished game warm the review's workers with a short search before Review is clicked?
items.body: Each review worker's first position costs about 190 ms more than the rest. RW1 made the workers early with no search and the review got no faster (×1.023, ab-20261020-1303-rw1.md), so the cost is not the worker's start-up. What is left is the JIT warming up, which needs a small search (about 5k nodes) to run before the click. The comment in GameView.tsx says the review never runs on its own, to spare a phone's battery.
items.recommend: Keep the rule for now. Allow one measurement patch that times a late position first, to split the 190 ms between the JIT and the start position, before deciding.

items.title: PR1 road (d): may the lobby and the game share one canvas, with a cut in place of the cross-fade?
items.body: Joining's first board picture takes about 880 ms. Traces show the wait is the GPU drawing each shader program for the first time in the game's new WebGL context: 14–150 ms per program under SwiftShader, paid again in each context (tools/jit-probe.mjs, rerun in this stage: link 1–4 ms, first draw 15–152 ms). The 23 programs the lobby and the game share would be drawn once if the game drew into the lobby's canvas. That changes the lobby invariant in CLAUDE.md: the lobby's canvas would no longer fade off the game's; the handover would be a cut on the frame both already show. Estimate, not measured: joining 880 → 200–350 ms. It is high risk and not built.
items.recommend: Allow a prototype on its own branch that first times its riskiest step (Stage and a starting board rendered by the lobby's renderer at the click). Decide on the handover's look with recordings in hand.

scoreboard.intro: The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. Each bar is a row's median pair, head divided by base; below 1 means faster. The dashed line is the target, 1.2× faster than the base. The branch's app code is the base's, so the step-2 A/B is also where the branch stands. The long view against the first recorded run was not re-measured: nothing changed to move it.

items.title: Step 2: the base against the last run's base, all 16 primary rows
items.body:
4bdeb55 against bd26e1c, 10 pairs, 74 minutes (ab-20261020-1303-regress.md): ×0.999 over 16 rows, none called either way; 117 diagnostics, none called. Memory flat (JS heap after reopening +0.2%). Start page bytes −0.3 KiB desktop, −0.4 KiB phone.

Where the time goes on the base: joining's first picture 880 ms, the computer's 912 ms, the review 2.04 s, reopening 165 ms, the player's move 159 ms, the opponent's 80 ms, a pick 82 ms, search 24.8 ms.

items.title: #201's leans read again
items.body: 4bdeb55 against 4b47d81 (main before #201), cold load, reopening and the review, 10 pairs (ab-20261020-1303-pr201.md). Reopening ×0.882: the ×1.167 lean seen before does not hold. The desktop first click went 10.8 → 14.2 ms (×1.286, 9 of 10 pairs worse, one at 0.74, not called). In the same runs the lobby's scene drew 819 → 515 ms after that click (×0.63, called better). Under full motion the side choice's words wait for that scene, so the player sees the way in about 300 ms sooner. The ledger's 0008:LC1 holds the follow-up.

items.body: The lobby's first frame came about 250 ms sooner, but the Join click then landed while the lobby still held the GPU. Joining 888 → 967 ms ×1.113 (8 of 10 pairs worse), and its longest freeze 127 → 633 ms, called worse (ab-20261020-1303-lz-setup.md).

items.title: RW1: make the review's workers once a finished game is on screen
items.body: The review went 2.02 → 2.07 s, ×1.023 (9 of 10 pairs at 1.00 or above; ab-20261020-1303-rw1.md). The first position's extra 190 ms per worker is not the worker starting up. See RW2 under Needs from me.

items.title: DC1: draw a move's or a pick's picture in its own React commit
items.body: Stopped before an A/B. One probe run handed the pictures to the GPU no sooner: the frame pacer holds the frame until the GPU finishes the previous one. Nothing was saved.

items.title: PR1: make the game's renderer and programs before the click (cut to one road)
items.body: Its riskiest step failed. A guest who waits 3 s before clicking Join gets the first picture in 277–294 ms, against 888–900 ms with no wait (2 runs each, ab-20261020-1303-pr1-probe.md). So the bench's wait is the lobby's own first frame still on the GPU, and a second context made earlier cannot help. Only one shared canvas could (road d, under Needs from me).

items.title: Two search micro-changes
items.body: 528 moves per ply and a break in quiescence's delta pruning: a node probe showed mixed or no change. Never committed.

items.title: No A/B on the final commit
items.body: The branch's app code is byte-identical to the base's, so a final A/B would be an A/A test. /check passed on the final commit: lint, build, 1,583 client tests with coverage, 80 server tests and both codegen gates. e2e was not run, because no UI, socket or protocol code changed.

items.title: LL2 and the search stack parked, not kept
items.body: Both leaned faster in most pairs but the A/B did not call them. A speed run keeps only called wins.

items.title: The JIT probe kept and fixed rather than removed
items.body: It is the only rerunnable evidence for the per-context first-draw cost that PR1's re-scoping rests on.

items.title: Trace times behind PR1
items.body: The join trace times (the click at about 960 ms after navigation, the game's first frame drawn at about 2.4 s, the no-linkAhead drawn times) come from single traces that were not saved. The no-linkAhead runs used a temporary client edit that was not saved either.

items.title: HF1's and LL2's triangle counts
items.body: They come from one run's raw data, since overwritten. Counts for the same ply vary between 47k and 76k from run to run, so HF1's estimate needs its own measurement.
